title: VP, Global Developer Relations
descriptionHtml:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

As our VP of Global Developer Relations, you’ll be the voice and facilitator of Mistral to the developer, scientific, and technical communities. You’ll build and scale a global DevRel strategy that fosters deep engagement, advocacy, and love for Mistral’s models and technology. Your team will build communities and educate, excite, and empower developers to adopt, innovate, and evangelize Mistral’s technology—whether they’re startups, enterprises, researchers, or open-source contributors.

You’ll work closely with Product, Research, Engineering, Marketing, Communications, and more to ensure developers have the tools, resources, and inspiration they need to succeed with Mistral.

What You Will Do

Build a Global Developer Movement

  • Develop and execute a global DevRel strategy that connects Mistral and our AI platform effectively with developers, scientists, and technologists.

  • Create authentic, developer-first engagement—focusing on education, inspiration, and community, with great content and AI tools.

  • Foster a culture of advocacy where developers naturally champion Mistral in their networks, projects, and conversations.

Engage and Inspire the Technical Community

  • Lead high-impact developer engagement initiatives, including:

    • Technical content (e.g., tutorials, blog posts, videos, documentation) that helps developers get started, optimize, and innovate with Mistral’s models.

    • Community programs (e.g., hackathons, meetups, AMAs, Discord/Slack communities) that bring together AI builders, researchers, and enthusiasts.

    • Evangelism & thought leadership (e.g., conference talks, podcasts, technical deep dives) that showcase Mistral’s unique value and capabilities.

  • Work with Product and Research teams to translate complex AI innovations into accessible, exciting, and actionable insights for developers.

Enable Developer Success, particularly for self-service adoption

  • Build scalable enablement programs (e.g., onboarding guides, SDKs, APIs, sample projects) that reduce friction for developers adopting Mistral’s models.

  • Create feedback loops between the developer community and Mistral’s Product/Engineering teams to shape the roadmap based on real-world needs.

Scale a World-Class DevRel Team

  • Hire, mentor, and lead a global team of Developer Advocates, Engineers and Evangelists - with particular strength in Europe and San Francisco

  • Define metrics and KPIs to measure the impact of DevRel (e.g., developer adoption, community growth, engagement, advocacy).

  • Lead from the front as a fantastic representative of Mistral at events, in social, and in project communities

Drive Open Source & Ecosystem Growth

  • Champion open-source contributions and collaborative innovation around Mistral’s models.

  • Partner with startups, enterprises, and academic institutions to accelerate adoption and co-innovation.

  • Identify and nurture key developer influencers, maintainers, and ambassadors who can amplify Mistral’s reach and impact.

What We're Looking For

  • Proven leadership in Developer Relations, Developer Marketing, or Technical Evangelism for a B2B technology company, preferably in AI, cloud, and open-source.

  • Deep technical credibility—ability to engage with developers, scientists, and engineers on their terms (e.g., code, research, architecture).

  • Passion for community building—a track record of growing and nurturing technical communities (e.g., open-source projects, developer forums, hackathons).

  • Strong storytelling and communication skills—ability to simplify complex concepts and inspire developers through content, talks, and interactions.

  • Strategic and operational excellence—ability to scale DevRel globally while maintaining a hands-on, authentic approach.

  • Collaborative mindset—ability to work across Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Sales to align DevRel with Mistral’s broader goals.

Bonus Points If You Have

  • Experience in AI, machine learning, or large language models (LLMs).

  • Personally contributed meaningfully to open source projects and communities.

  • Led global DevRel teams in high-growth, competitive markets.

  • Personal brand or following in the developer or AI community Experience launching and scaling developer-focused products or tools.

Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

title: Working Student - ML Compiler
descriptionHtml:
On-site | Part-time (20 hours per week)

About Tensordyne 

Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence!

The Opportunity

At Tensordyne, we are at the forefront of cutting-edge AI hardware and software solutions. To keep pace in this dynamic, interdisciplinary field, we are seeking a Working Student in ML Compiler Engineering to contribute to the development of compilers for our custom ASICs.

This role offers an exciting opportunity to gain hands-on experience in full-stack compiler engineering while working alongside a team of experts in a fast-paced, innovative environment. If you are passionate about machine learning compilers, numerical programming, and performance optimization, we’d love to hear from you!

As a working student, you’ll gain valuable experience in a dynamic and innovative environment that thrives on curiosity and collaboration. This part-time role (20 hours per week) is based on-site at our Munich office..

The specific duties of this role will be shaped by both our business priorities and your individual interests.

Your Responsibilities

  • Design and implement ML compiler passes and optimizations tailored for our custom ASIC architecture.
  • Develop intuitive tooling to elevate the developer experience of our production ML compiler.
  • Work closely with multi-disciplinary teams, ranging from ML to embedded system engineers.

What you'll bring 

  • A highly motivated, curious, and detail-oriented mindset with a strong desire to learn.
  • Passion for compilers
  • Solid understanding of graph theory and graph algorithms.
  • Proficiency in at least one systems programming language (e.g., C++, Rust).
  • Experience with Python and its ecosystem.
  • Currently enrolled in a Master's program in Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related AI field.

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with parallel programming frameworks such as CUDA or OpenMP.
  • Interest in programming language design and compiler theory.
  • Experience with performance optimization.

Tensordyne's culture was built on the following values:

  • Put people first. We only succeed when our people succeed.
  • Ethics and integrity always; Being open, honest, and respectful of everyone.
  • Think Big. Be ambitious and have audacious goals.
  • Aim for excellence. Quality and excellence count in everything we do.
  • Own it and get it done. Results matter!
  • Make each person better together, than they would be as an individual.
  • Embrace each others’ differences, and embrace that there will be differences.

Tensordyne is an equal opportunity employer. We believe that a diverse team is better at tackling complex problems and coming up with innovative solutions. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, race, religion, pregnancy, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.

title: Workplace Technology Lead
descriptionHtml:
Mission

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear.

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

As the Workplace Technology Lead you'll be the domain expert and technical authority for workplace technology and AV innovation within Corporate Engineering. Setting technical direction, leading technology delivery for capital builds, and creating and owning repeatable standards that support employees, clinicians and members.

This is a senior technical leadership role, so you'll deliver by influencing, coordinating and partnering across the organisation (Engineering, Facilities, Clinical, Real Estate). It combines hands-on delivery, programme leadership and practical AI solutions, and you'll shape how the function grows as Neko expands.

Your scope covers collaboration and meeting spaces, employee experience, executive briefing centres, clinic environmental AV and debrief-room presentation, digital signage, and technology integration across a growing portfolio of health centres. Network, security, facilities, clinical systems and scanning hardware stay with their specialist owners, and you'll work closely with them.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • Map the estate, opening pipeline, suppliers, ownership and risks in your first 60 days, and agree the role charter, roadmap and budget baseline with Technology and Operations

  • Create a global technology roadmap aligned to expansion plans, workplace needs and the member experience, turned into investment priorities, delivery plans and lifecycle budgets

  • Act as design authority for workplace and AV: define reference designs, preferred solutions and a clear process for local variations

  • Review existing standards, take full ownership of them in Corporate Engineering, and create a repeatable technology build playbook, piloted on an agreed site or room type

  • Lead the technology workstream for new offices, health centres and refurbishments, from feasibility and design through procurement, commissioning and operational handover

  • Own the integrated technology programme: financial forecasts, risks, changes and executive reporting, with clear readiness criteria, acceptance tests and defect tracking for each opening

  • Work with clinical operations and design teams on debrief displays, ambient audio, signage and controls, prioritising simple use, discretion and a calm environment for members

  • Test two approved operational AI use cases, for example automated commissioning tools, through measured pilots

  • Establish asset and lifecycle records, supplier reviews and service requirements with Procurement and support owners

  • Deliver a costed proposal and an 18–24 month plan for the next stage of the function, with any hiring linked to the site pipeline and support demand

What We're Looking For

  • Substantial experience in workplace technology, enterprise AV and integrated systems, including delivery across multiple countries and physical environments

  • A record of technical leadership: setting standards across a complex portfolio and developing others through influence rather than line authority

  • Experience taking technology projects through architectural design, procurement, construction, commissioning and handover, with commercial and programme accountability

  • Ability to explain technical decisions to executives, clinicians, designers and delivery partners, and to connect investment choices to practical user needs

  • Practical curiosity about AI and automation, with the judgement to test outputs and involve specialist owners

Nice to Have

  • Healthcare or regulated-environment experience

  • Enterprise and experiential delivery experience

Equal Opportunity and Inclusion

Neko Health is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are happy to make reasonable adjustments throughout the hiring process.
